properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/26/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Leroy Twp, Bradford county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 973524
Permit API: 015-23687
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/26/2022
Comments: Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake, Environmental) called the DEP yesterday afternoon to report a metal waste oil tote fell off a forklift and ruptured. It leaked an estimated 30 gallons of oil onto the pad surface. I spoke with Aaron Stredny (Chesapeake) on site who showed me where the spill occurred on the north end of the pad. The oil spilled on top of a water puddle and floated on the water. A vac truck removed the oil immediately after the spill. Then a skid steer scraped ~1" of the pad surface in approximately 100'x100' area and placed ~11 tons of pad material on liner containment. They finished the cleanup about 1 hour after the spill.Creston Environmental is screening the spill area today with a MiniRae 3000 photoionization detector (PID) and collecting confirmatory soil samples. I used a MiniRae 3000 with a 10.6 eV bulb to screen test holes in the excavated area. The highest reading was 0.7 ppm, indicating a negligible presence of volatiles in the pad material. I spoke with Aaron Vaughn (Chesapeake, HSE). He explained the oil spill was gear oil drained from equipment on site.I spoke with Marty Balada (Chesapeake, Company Man). He explained the 4 Marcellus wells here are already hydraulically fractured. Cudd's coil tubing unit started drilling out the plugs yesterday; they expect to finish drilling plugs in about 8 days.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water of 3 separate puddles on the pad surface have electrical conductivity of 0.40-0.55 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35.Violations cited to the 015-23687 well permit are considered immediately corrected. Air temp 59FJLP

Operator failed to submit an annual mechanical integrity report to the Department for the year 2022. Violations of section 78.88 have occurred.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/12/2024 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Cherry Township, Sullivan county. OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/12/2024
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 8207458
Permit API: 113-20465
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/12/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted by EPS Justin Abbott at the Yonkin Well Pad in response to a spill notification submitted by CHK (aka Expand Energy) for a spill detected at 1300 hours on 11/11/24. Meeting on site today with CHK Consultant Brett Fowler. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 39 degrees F. According to the Emergency Response Notification Report at 1300 hours the following occurred, "up welling of pad adjacent to well head caused concern; Expand started digging at on 11/11/24 at 1:00 p.m.; Expand Energy started digging and encountered produced water with a conductivity of 8000 s/cm. Source of produced water is unknown. Ms. Schaad said that the produced water was not coming up from around the well casing. Expand Energy has Creston Environmental on site utilizing a vac truck to empty excavation. Ms. Schaad said that a small volume of produced water (greater than 5 gallons) has been recovered."At time of inspection, the Department observed a trench dug adjacent to the 5HC well in the affected area. The Department conducted conductivity screenings of the affected area using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Puddled fluid collected in the trench in the affected area was observed with electrical conductivity readings of 3.24 mS/cm. The trenched area of the reported spill was approximately 12' long by 6' wide and 4' deep where water is puddled (photo 4). In a followup conversation with Danielle Schaad, HSE Representative for Chesapeake, the following information was relayed regarding the cause of the spill: the spill of production fluid was observed to be caused by a torn seam in the secondary containment structure which was not apparent until rig mats and containment were removed. Approximately one barrel of fluid was vacuumed from the trench and 14 cubic yards of impacted pad rock were removed from the trench. CHK has contracted with Creston Environmental to pursue Act 2 site characterization. According to Mr. Fowler, Nine Energy Services is conducting wireline operations to change out a valve on the 23HC well (API#113-20465). Plugs have been drilled out, but the wells are shut in and no production equipment has yet been set up on this pad. Rig mats are also observed being stacked and removed from the location at time of inspection. A supersucker vacuum truck is observed on site removing high conductivity fluids from the impacted rock stockpiled in the northwest corner of the pad (photo 5). Additional puddles with elevated conductivity readings ranging from 2.2-2.7 mS/cm were observed (photo 6) where impacted pad rock is stockpiled. The Department recommends vacuuming fluid from surface puddles adjacent to the stockpile. During site walk, the Department inspected downslope areas of the well pad to determine if fluid was released from the pad surface. No indication of off-pad release was observed. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding against API# 113-20470 for SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) dated 9/23/24.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/28/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 987252
Permit API: 015-22203
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/07/2023
Comments: On 3/7/2023, DEP representatives John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Maggie well site. This inspection is to report the results of a water sample that was collected from a water puddle on the west corner of the Maggie well site.During an inspection on 12/28/2022, the department discovered high conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 50' x 50' area and was field tested in different areas with results being >20.0 mS. 20.0 mS is the upper limit of the Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected a sample of the water for laboratory analysis from location N 41.684052 W -76.121972.On 2/22/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated aluminum, barium, iron, magnesium, sodium, strontium, and chlorides and is indicative of regulated substances being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 1 and 2. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3482654 for high conductance fluid being discovered on the pad surface.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 924088
Permit API: 129-26518
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/19/2021
Comments: On July 19, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz 1 oil and gas well in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted in response to a reportable release received on 7/19/2021. On 7/19/2021, the Operator reported that a landowner hit a valve while mowing on Friday July 16, 2021 and did not notify the Operator emergency number. The Operator located the voice mail on 7/19/2021 and responded immediately. I spoke with Marc Jacobs regarding the release. Mr. Jacobs indicated that approximately 40 barrels of fluid was lost from the brine tank. Additionally, Mike Walor Woodard & Curran was contracted to evaluate and remediate the impacted area. Mr. Walor indicated that the impacted material would be remediated in accordance with the Act 2 standards. At the time of inspection, The Operator was removing fluid from the fiberglass brine tank with a vac truck. I observed a significant amount of crude oil and brine spilled to the ground and resulted in a flow path approximately 500’ down gradient from the well through the landowners mowed field. The spill appeared to emanate at or near the brine tank valve. I spoke with the landowner, who admitted to hitting the valve with the mower deck on Friday July 16, 2021. The landowner also indicated that it was raining when the valve was struck. The impacted material was not observed in or appeared to have entered waters of the commonwealth. In addition to the spill, the fiberglass brine tank appeared to have been previously leaking and repaired prior to the release. A vertical dark stripe was visible on the side of the fiberglass below what appeared to be two fiberglass patches applied to the brine tank. The Department is seeking clarification on when the patches were applied and why the patched were needed. I recommend that the Operator design, construct, maintain, and reasonably protect the brine tank from unauthorized acts of third parties. The fluid lost also appears to be crude oil. The Department is seeking clarification in regard to the amount of crude oil contained within the brine tank as the brine tank was not equipped with secondary containment. Violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further investigation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/30/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8202743
Permit API: 015-23828
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/30/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite for a routine inspection. It was about 73F and overcast.There were 5 active wells, 1 plugged well, 1 GPU, 5 separators, 1 produced fluid tank, and 1 temporary storage tank onsite. The site was vegetated and appeared stable. There were no erosion or sedimentation issues noted. A filter strip was installed as PCSM on the western side of the pad. The PCSM appeared to be functioning properly.At least 3 puddles were observed on the pad surface near the produced fluid tank (Photos 4 and 6). These puddles and the water in the produced fluid tank secondary containment were screened for conductivity. The conductivity readings ranged from about 5 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) to about 7 mS/cm, both in containment and on the pad. The readings averaged about 6.5 mS/cm (Photo 3). Due to the elevated conductivity of the puddles, sample 0719-286 was collected from the largest puddle (Photo 5).Other puddles on the pad surface were screened and had conductivity readings around 0.5 mS/cm. The PCSM and surrounding areas were screened visually and with a soil conductivity meter. There did not appear to be any visual impacts and the soil conductivity readings ranged between 0.01 mS/cm and 0.1 mS/cm.Due to the unknown volume, origin, and time of the release, it is strongly recommended that remediation be completed under Act 2 requirements. Additional screening should also be performed on and around the pad to determine the extent of potential additional impacts. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b). Additional violations may be cited based on the pending results of sample 0719-286.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8278800
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/23/2026
Comments: On 6/23/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of four liquid samples that were collected during fracking operations from four locations at the site. During inspection #4183490 conducted on 4/21/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface, in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad and in liquid flowing past the LOD. Samples were collected from four locations. On 6/18/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, field tested at 9.40 mS conductance. Sample 9551-242 was collected from the puddle. Reference pictures 1, 2, and 3.Liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad field tested at 10.30 mS conductance. Sample 9551-243 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 4, 5, and 6.Liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Sample 9551-244 was collected from the pond. Reference pictures 7, 8, and 9.Liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD field tested at 3.33 mS conductance. Sample 9551-245 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 10, 11, and 12.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.

The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20"x 13 3/8") annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20" x13 3/8") annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve (Sentry replaced with bull plug for testing). Both wells remained in production through the SPBUT period. All annuli of each well have been shut in for testing. The (20"x13") annulus was shut in for 72hrs., the (13"x9") annuli were shut in for 48hrs. and the (9"x5") annuli were shut in for 24hrs. resulting in SPBUTs. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. (John Pazzaglia) and Creston Consultant Reps. (Jason Rajan and Tiffany Smith). Starting at approx. 10:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 8/11/22). Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 0 psi.; 10% gas; Sample taken @ 10:05 - (9x5): 361 psi.; 100% gas; Sample taken @ 10:10 - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 0 psi.; 0% gas; No sample taken * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 2.2 psi.; 88% gas; Sample taken @ 10:21 - (9x5); 127 psi.; 96% gas; Sample taken @ 10:27 - All annuli were returned to venting by 10:30

Comments: On August 6 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County. At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the affected area of the pump jack fluid release documented in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. There were erosion and sedimentation issues at the well site and adjacent to the wellhead due to the prior releases of the fluid from the pump jack onto the ground in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. It appears the erosion that previously extended adjacent to and downslope from the well site is now exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage with the exception of the area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead. A background soil conductivity reading was taken. The soil conductivity reading was 0.0370mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the wellhead. Comments: On 10/18/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Drugman Unit well site for violations cited on 3/24/2023 (SAIR 352558, Enforcement ID: 415452, CID 370524). But as of the 10/18/23 follow up inspection, the level spreader had not been installed at the outlet of Culvert #7. Along with the calculations and supporting documents to show compliance with Chapter 102.8, please provide an update regarding the proposed level spreader and ensure that the concentration of flows at the outlet of Culvert #7 is not causing a nuisance. Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/31/2023
Comments: On August 31 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Adams 877-5 OG Well. The findings were as follows:The well site was located in an open field. The access road appeared stabilized at the time of this inspection. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. Upon inspection of the production tank there appeared to be a corroded valve near the base of the tank. Further inspection of this valve showed signs of apparent staining in the gravel, indicating a leak. Soil conductivity readings were taken under and near the valve and indicated elevated levels of contaminants with readings of 5.08mS, 4.86mS, and 2.79mS. Based on these observations, the Department recommends the operator assess the integrity of the production tank and corresponding production equipment, as well as assess the well site for leaks or spills and notify the Department of the findings within 10 days of receiving this inspection report. The Department is requesting the following information:1: What was released?2: When the release occurred?3: How long was the release occurring?4:Why the release occurred?5: The quantity of the release and how the quantity was determined?Based on today's inspection, violations 78.57 (a), 78.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. It rained steadily during this inspection. Tobias had already scraped a thin layer of gravel off of the top of the impacted area at the time of inspection. Mr. Lee said that Creston Environmental was also present to take samples and characterize the release. Some areas of the impacted pad area were more damp than others. No standing fluid was observed in this area of the well pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material according to the Hanna soil conductivity meter ranged from 0.41 mS/cm to 2.86 mS/cm. The higher EC readings were found closer to the well heads and the lower readings were taken farther away from the well heads toward the southeast pad edge. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted.Violations remain outstanding for the release from June 1, 2026. These violations will be closed upon demonstration of Act 2 remediation standards.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 1/26/2024
Violation Code: 78a65(e)1-7 - SITE RESTORATION – Post drilling restoration reports – Operator failed to electronically submit an administratively complete restoration report to the Department.
Violation ID: 8173301
Permit API: 125-28695
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 1/26/2024
Comments: On 1/26/2024, I conducted a restoration inspection at the Hunter Well Site in response to a Post Drilling Restoration Report submitted by the Operator on 12/1/2023. The date of the final well drilled or expired: 12/31/2019.The ESCGP was terminated on 11/4/2022. The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-The Emergence Response Plan was on site.-Well head appeared to be in good condition and well tag was present (Photo 16).-Well equipment, production tanks and GPUs appeared to be in good condition.-Production fluid tanks placed with secondary containment.-The GPUs appeared to be equipped with secondary containment and low conductivity fluid was observed under the GPUs.-Drilling equipment and machinery appeared to be removed from site (Photo 16).-Generally, the site appeared to be vegetated and restored, however two erosion rills were observed (Photo 4). I recommend that the Operator backfill, regrade, seed, mulch and temporary stabilize the rills until permanently stabilized with vegetation. -The PCSM feature was not holding water (Photo7). Neither the forebay nor the main basin appeared to be holding water. No water was observed discharging from the basin outlets (Photo 8). An excavated or collapsed hole was observed near the PCSM riser. A corrugated black plastic pipe was visible in the excavated or collapsed hole near the PCSM basin riser (Photo 9 and 10).
